293: ## AI EXECUTION PROTOCOL
294: 
295: Written for the executing swarm. Follow each rule as written. Where a rule and your own judgment disagree, follow the rule and record the disagreement in `goal.md` section 4.
296: 
297: ### Roles
298: - **Conductor**: one DeepSeek V4.1 Flash max session that is not itself running inside OpenCode, because `cli-opencode` refuses a dispatch from inside OpenCode. It dispatches workers, runs every verify command, edits only this phase folder, and keeps `goal.md` section 4 current.
299: - **Worker**: one `opencode2 run` dispatch on `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max`. One worker does one lane or one baseline run, then stops.
300: - **Reviewer**: one read-only frontier review through `cli-codex` at phase close. It writes nothing.
301: 
302: ### Pre-Task Checklist
303: - [ ] Read this phase's `spec.md`, this plan and `tasks.md` before the first dispatch
304: - [ ] Read `.skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/SKILL.md` sections 3 and 4 before composing the first worker command
305: - [ ] Confirm the working directory is the build worktree recorded in `../goal.md` section 4, never the main checkout
306: - [ ] Confirm `opencode2 models --standalone` lists `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`
307: - [ ] Save every brief to `scratch/briefs/<task-id>.txt` before dispatching it
308: 
309: ### Execution Rules
310: 
311: | Rule | Requirement |
312: |------|-------------|
313: | TASK-SEQ | Run tasks in ID order. Tasks marked `[P]` may run together, at most three at once, and only when no two write the same file |
314: | TASK-SCOPE | A worker writes only the paths under ALLOWED WRITE PATHS in its brief |
315: | TASK-VERIFY | The conductor runs the task's verify command and reads both its output and its exit status before marking the task `[x]` |
316: | TASK-LOCATE | Find text by its exact content, never by a line number |
317: | TASK-BANNED | Workers never run `git commit`, `git push`, `git checkout`, `git switch`, `git branch`, `git reset`, `git stash`, `generate-context.js` or `/speckit:save` |
318: 
319: ### Worker Brief Skeleton
320: 
321: Every brief starts with this block, word for word, with the two paths filled in:
322: 
323: ```text
324: GATE 3 IS PRE-RESOLVED. DO NOT ASK THE DOCUMENTATION-SCOPE QUESTION.
325: 
326: You are a non-interactive dispatched worker. AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 and
327: SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0 are set in your environment, which this repository's AGENTS.md
328: defines as the autonomous child-dispatch exemption: the spec-folder question is pre-resolved
329: and MUST NOT be asked. No answer can reach you, because nobody is at a prompt.
330: 
331: Your write authority is already bound. The spec folder is:
332:   specs/system-speckit/054-weak-model-spec-authoring/001-template-drift-census-and-baseline
333: 
334: Proceed directly to the work. Do not print A/B/C/D options. Do not stop to confirm anything.
335: A failed edit match means a stale anchor: re-read the file and retry; halt only after three
336: failures on the same file.
337: Your task is complete only when files exist on disk and the verification command has been run.
338: 
339: ROLE: You are a read-only auditor. You read files, run read-only commands and write one
340: result file. Your output is checked line by line by a script.
341: 
342: ALLOWED WRITE PATHS:
343:   <the one file this task names>
344: 
345: BANNED OPERATIONS: git commit, git push, git checkout, git switch, git branch, git reset,
346: git stash, rm, mv, create.sh outside the task's stated command, generate-context.js,
347: /speckit:save, and any edit to a file not listed under ALLOWED WRITE PATHS.
348: ```
349: 
350: The role line is a focused persona summary in place of a full agent file, the small-context exception that `cli-opencode` rule 18 allows. It is declared here as that exception.
351: 
352: ### Dispatch Command
353: 
354: ```bash
355: cd "$WORKTREE" && SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0 AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 opencode2 run --standalone \
356:   -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max --format json \
357:   "$(cat "$PHASE/scratch/briefs/$TASK.txt")" </dev/null > "$PHASE/scratch/runs/$TASK.jsonl" 2>&1 &
358: PID=$!; wait "$PID"; kill -9 "$PID" 2>/dev/null; pkill -9 -P "$PID" 2>/dev/null
359: ```
360: 
361: `PHASE` is this folder's path and `WORKTREE` is the build worktree. Never kill by a name pattern. Kill only the captured PID.
362: 
363: ### Status Reporting Format
364: 
365: `[T###] DONE | BLOCKED - one line of evidence`, written as a row in the progress table of `goal.md` section 4.
366: 
367: ### Blocked Task Protocol
368: 1. Restore any file the task changed with `git restore --source=<start commit> -- <file>`.
369: 2. Mark the task `[B]` in `tasks.md` with the failing command and the first line of its output.
370: 3. Re-dispatch at most twice with the brief corrected for what failed. After the third failure on the same task, leave it `[B]` and continue with the next task.
371: 4. Stop the phase when two tasks are blocked, and write `STOP` with both task IDs in `goal.md` section 4.
372: <!-- /ANCHOR:ai-execution -->

376: ## L3: ARCHITECTURE DECISION RECORD
377: 
378: ### ADR-001: Keep only rows that reproduce
379: 
380: **Status**: Accepted
381: 
382: **Context**: A DeepSeek worker asked to find defects will also report things that are not defects.
383: 
384: **Decision**: A lane row enters `ledger.jsonl` only when the conductor runs its `evidence_cmd` on the unchanged tree and the output contains its `evidence_expect`. The `self-contradiction` class has no command, so those rows go to the frontier review instead.
385: 
386: **Consequences**:
387: - Phase 2 receives no row it cannot reproduce.
388: - A real defect the worker described badly is dropped. The frontier review reads the source files again to catch those.
389: 
390: **Alternatives Rejected**:
391: - Trusting lane output as written: it puts unconfirmed findings into a repair phase that edits shared templates.
392: 
393: ### ADR-002: One fixed authoring task, three runs, run in a throwaway track
394: 
395: **Status**: Accepted
396: 
397: **Context**: The baseline must be rerun unchanged in phase 8, and one run of a sampling model is one sample.
398: 
399: **Decision**: The task text in `tasks.md` T009 is frozen. It runs three times per side. Each run creates `specs/zz-bench-authoring/`, and the conductor deletes that directory after measuring.
400: 
401: **Consequences**:
402: - Phase 8 compares like with like and reports a range.
403: - Three runs cannot detect a small effect. Phase 8 reports the range, not a significance claim.
404: 
405: **Alternatives Rejected**:
406: - Measuring by a frontier model's judgment of quality: one model is one opinion, and the five metrics are commands.

280: ## L3: MILESTONES
281: 
282: | Milestone | Description | Success Criteria | Target |

293: ## AI EXECUTION PROTOCOL
294: 
295: Written for the executing swarm. Follow each rule as written. Where a rule and your own judgment disagree, follow the rule and record the disagreement in `goal.md` section 4.
296: 
297: ### Roles
298: - **Conductor**: one DeepSeek V4.1 Flash max session that is not itself running inside OpenCode, because `cli-opencode` refuses a dispatch from inside OpenCode. It dispatches workers, runs every verify command, edits only this phase folder, and keeps `goal.md` section 4 current.
299: - **Worker**: one `opencode2 run` dispatch on `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max`. One worker does one lane or one baseline run, then stops.
300: - **Reviewer**: one read-only frontier review through `cli-codex` at phase close. It writes nothing.
301: 
302: ### Pre-Task Checklist
303: - [ ] Read this phase's `spec.md`, this plan and `tasks.md` before the first dispatch
304: - [ ] Read `.skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/SKILL.md` sections 3 and 4 before composing the first worker command
305: - [ ] Confirm the working directory is the build worktree recorded in `../goal.md` section 4, never the main checkout
306: - [ ] Confirm `opencode2 models --standalone` lists `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`
307: - [ ] Save every brief to `scratch/briefs/<task-id>.txt` before dispatching it
308: 
309: ### Execution Rules
310: 
311: | Rule | Requirement |
312: |------|-------------|
313: | TASK-SEQ | Run tasks in ID order. Tasks marked `[P]` may run together, at most three at once, and only when no two write the same file |
314: | TASK-SCOPE | A worker writes only the paths under ALLOWED WRITE PATHS in its brief |
315: | TASK-VERIFY | The conductor runs the task's verify command and reads both its output and its exit status before marking the task `[x]` |
316: | TASK-LOCATE | Find text by its exact content, never by a line number |
317: | TASK-BANNED | Workers never run `git commit`, `git push`, `git checkout`, `git switch`, `git branch`, `git reset`, `git stash`, `generate-context.js` or `/speckit:save` |
318: 
319: ### Worker Brief Skeleton
320: 
321: Every brief starts with this block, word for word, with the two paths filled in:
322: 
323: ```text
324: GATE 3 IS PRE-RESOLVED. DO NOT ASK THE DOCUMENTATION-SCOPE QUESTION.
325: 
326: You are a non-interactive dispatched worker. AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 and
327: SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0 are set in your environment, which this repository's AGENTS.md
328: defines as the autonomous child-dispatch exemption: the spec-folder question is pre-resolved
329: and MUST NOT be asked. No answer can reach you, because nobody is at a prompt.
330: 
331: Your write authority is already bound. The spec folder is:
332:   specs/system-speckit/054-weak-model-spec-authoring/001-template-drift-census-and-baseline
333: 
334: Proceed directly to the work. Do not print A/B/C/D options. Do not stop to confirm anything.
335: A failed edit match means a stale anchor: re-read the file and retry; halt only after three
336: failures on the same file.
337: Your task is complete only when files exist on disk and the verification command has been run.
338: 
339: ROLE: You are a read-only auditor. You read files, run read-only commands and write one
340: result file. Your output is checked line by line by a script.
341: 
342: ALLOWED WRITE PATHS:
343:   <the one file this task names>
344: 
345: BANNED OPERATIONS: git commit, git push, git checkout, git switch, git branch, git reset,
346: git stash, rm, mv, create.sh outside the task's stated command, generate-context.js,
347: /speckit:save, and any edit to a file not listed under ALLOWED WRITE PATHS.
348: ```
349: 
350: The role line is a focused persona summary in place of a full agent file, the small-context exception that `cli-opencode` rule 18 allows. It is declared here as that exception.
351: 
352: ### Dispatch Command
353: 
354: ```bash
355: cd "$WORKTREE" && SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0 AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 opencode2 run --standalone \
356:   -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max --format json \
357:   "$(cat "$PHASE/scratch/briefs/$TASK.txt")" </dev/null > "$PHASE/scratch/runs/$TASK.jsonl" 2>&1 &
358: PID=$!; wait "$PID"; kill -9 "$PID" 2>/dev/null; pkill -9 -P "$PID" 2>/dev/null
359: ```
360: 
361: `PHASE` is this folder's path and `WORKTREE` is the build worktree. Never kill by a name pattern. Kill only the captured PID.
362: 
363: ### Status Reporting Format
364: 
365: `[T###] DONE | BLOCKED - one line of evidence`, written as a row in the progress table of `goal.md` section 4.
366: 
367: ### Blocked Task Protocol
368: 1. Restore any file the task changed with `git restore --source=<start commit> -- <file>`.
369: 2. Mark the task `[B]` in `tasks.md` with the failing command and the first line of its output.
370: 3. Re-dispatch at most twice with the brief corrected for what failed. After the third failure on the same task, leave it `[B]` and continue with the next task.
371: 4. Stop the phase when two tasks are blocked, and write `STOP` with both task IDs in `goal.md` section 4.
372: <!-- /ANCHOR:ai-execution -->
373: 
374: ---
375: 
376: ## L3: ARCHITECTURE DECISION RECORD
377: 
378: ### ADR-001: Keep only rows that reproduce
379: 
380: **Status**: Accepted
381: 
382: **Context**: A DeepSeek worker asked to find defects will also report things that are not defects.
383: 
384: **Decision**: A lane row enters `ledger.jsonl` only when the conductor runs its `evidence_cmd` on the unchanged tree and the output contains its `evidence_expect`. The `self-contradiction` class has no command, so those rows go to the frontier review instead.
385: 
386: **Consequences**:
387: - Phase 2 receives no row it cannot reproduce.
388: - A real defect the worker described badly is dropped. The frontier review reads the source files again to catch those.
389: 
390: **Alternatives Rejected**:
391: - Trusting lane output as written: it puts unconfirmed findings into a repair phase that edits shared templates.
392: 
393: ### ADR-002: One fixed authoring task, three runs, run in a throwaway track
394: 
395: **Status**: Accepted
396: 
397: **Context**: The baseline must be rerun unchanged in phase 8, and one run of a sampling model is one sample.
398: 
399: **Decision**: The task text in `tasks.md` T009 is frozen. It runs three times per side. Each run creates `specs/zz-bench-authoring/`, and the conductor deletes that directory after measuring.
400: 
401: **Consequences**:
402: - Phase 8 compares like with like and reports a range.
403: - Three runs cannot detect a small effect. Phase 8 reports the range, not a significance claim.
404: 
405: **Alternatives Rejected**:
406: - Measuring by a frontier model's judgment of quality: one model is one opinion, and the five metrics are commands.
407:

6: # Sourced by validate.sh and compatible with strict mode.

9: # Rule: PLACEHOLDER_FILLED
10: # Severity: error
11: # Description: Detects unfilled spec-doc placeholders: [YOUR_VALUE_HERE:], [NEEDS_CLARIFICATION:] / [NEEDS CLARIFICATION:],
12: #   and a [template:...] provenance token left in a title line. Bracketed authoring hints such as [Decision Title]
13: #   are soft by design and belong to spec/check-placeholders.sh, the standalone report.
14: # Parity: mirrors the runtime orchestrator validatePlaceholders. Mustache {{...}} is NOT flagged
15: # (not canonical spec-doc placeholder syntax; legit spec-doc content uses it).
16: # The post-edit hook runs the broader bracket scan at spec/check-placeholders.sh
17: # instead; that one catches leftovers of upgrade-level, this one gates closure.
18: 
19: # ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
20: # 1. INITIALIZATION
21: # ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
22: 
23: run_check() {
24:     local folder="$1"
25:     local level="$2"
26:     
27:     RULE_NAME="PLACEHOLDER_FILLED"
28:     RULE_STATUS="pass"
29:     RULE_MESSAGE=""
30:     RULE_DETAILS=()
31:     RULE_REMEDIATION=""
32:     
33:     local -a files=("spec.md" "plan.md" "tasks.md")

35:

41: 
42:     for file in "${files[@]}"; do
43:         local filepath="$folder/$file"
44:         [[ ! -f "$filepath" ]] && continue
45:         
46:         # Skip: scratch/, memory/, templates/
47:         if [[ "$filepath" == *"/scratch/"* ]] || \
48:            [[ "$filepath" == *"/memory/"* ]] || \
49:            [[ "$filepath" == *"/templates/"* ]]; then
50:             continue

53:         if type -t should_skip_path &>/dev/null; then
54:             if should_skip_path "$filepath"; then
55:                 continue

56: ## 3. ARCHITECTURE
57: 
58: ### Pattern
59: A stamp-gated lifecycle. The template stamp says which contract a doc was written under. The validator keeps the old strict verdict for any doc without the new stamp and applies the Draft lifecycle only to docs that carry it.
60: 
61: ### Facts read from the tree while this plan was written
62: 
63: - `validate.sh` runs the compiled `runtime/dist/lib/validation/orchestrator.js`, never the shell rules, for the rule `PLACEHOLDER_FILLED`. The orchestrator lists it in `nativeRuleIds`, and `runRegistryShellRules` skips every rule in that set. The proof is the wording: a v2.3 scaffold validated in a scratch copy printed `unfilled value token(s) in a Draft packet`, which is the new orchestrator message, and not the shell message.
64: - `validate.sh` exits 3 with the text `compiled validation orchestrator is stale` when `runtime/dist` is older than its source. So the TypeScript edit is invisible until `npm run build` runs under `runtime/`.
65: - `rules/check-placeholders.sh` still matters. The harness `runtime/cli/tests/test-validation-extended.sh` sources it in the category `Individual Rule: PLACEHOLDER_FILLED (check-placeholders.sh)`, and its header says it mirrors the orchestrator.
66: - A warning does not fail strict. The orchestrator sets `passed: summary.errors === 0`.
67: - `create.sh` function `finalize_scaffold_templates` replaces `[NAME]`, `[YYYY-MM-DD]`, `[Feature Name]` and `[###-feature-name]` and strips ` [template:...]` with `perl`. Function `ensure_template_source_near_top` moves the stamp line below the frontmatter. The stamp text, including its version, comes from the template.
68: - `templates/spec-kit-docs.json` lists a version per template, and `runtime/cli/tests/template-version-parity.vitest.ts` fails when a manifest version differs from the template stamp.
69: - `runtime/cli/tests/scaffold-golden-snapshots.vitest.ts` renders these templates and compares them with `runtime/cli/tests/snapshots/scaffold-golden-snapshots.vitest.ts.snap`. Without `-u` it fails after conversion on four tests.
70: - The orchestrator reads every authored doc that is present. The shell rule reads only `spec.md`, `plan.md`, `tasks.md` and `decision-record.md`. This difference exists today and the plan keeps it for older docs (ADR-007).
71: 
72: ### Frozen definitions
73: 
74: **Hint.** A bracketed text that matches `\[[A-Za-z/][^]\[]{2,}\]`. The slash lets the score cells `[/25]`, `[/20]` and `[/15]` count. Phase 1 counted with a letter-only start, so on the same Level 2 scaffold it saw 97 occurrences and this regex sees 101.
75: 
76: **Conversion rule.** The script `convert_hints.py` turns a hint into `[YOUR_VALUE_HERE: ` followed by the hint text and `]`. The text keeps its case. It skips five cases:
77: 1. A line inside a fenced code block.
78: 2. Text inside an inline code span.
79: 3. Text followed directly by `(`, which is a link.
80: 4. The five scaffolder texts `NAME`, `Feature Name`, `YYYY-MM-DD`, `###-feature-name` and `1/2/3/3+`, and any text that starts with `template:`. `create.sh` replaces or strips them, so a token there would stay in every scaffold.
81: 5. A text that already starts with `YOUR_VALUE_HERE`.
82: 
83: **Counts the conversion must give.** Converted per file: `spec.md.tmpl` 96, `plan.md.tmpl` 90, `tasks.md.tmpl` 7, `implementation-summary.md.tmpl` 11, `acceptance-criteria.md.tmpl` 10, so 214 in all. The total hint count of each file does not change, because a token is itself a hint under this regex. The bare hints left are exactly the ones in `tasks.md` T011.
84: 
85: **Stamp.** The 7 stamp lines of those five templates change from `| v2.2 -->` to `| v2.3 -->`: 3 in `spec.md.tmpl` and 1 each in the other four. The five manifest entries change the same way.
86: 
87: **Gate stamp.** A doc carries the gate stamp when one of its first 70 lines matches `<!-- SPECKIT_TEMPLATE_SOURCE: <names> | vMAJOR.MINOR -->` with MAJOR above 2, or MAJOR 2 and MINOR 3 or more. A doc with an older stamp or none does not.
88: 
89: **Lifecycle.**
90: 
91: | Doc | Status in `spec.md` | Unfilled `[YOUR_VALUE_HERE:` token | `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION:` | Strict result |
92: |-----|---------------------|------------------------------------|-------------------------|---------------|
93: | Gate stamp | Draft | warning | error | passes when nothing else errors |
94: | Gate stamp | any other value or none | error | error | fails |
95: | No gate stamp | any value | error | error | fails, as before |
96: 
97: Draft means the cell holds the word Draft, ignoring case, bold marks, backticks, outer quotes, trailing punctuation and repeated spaces. The first Status row of the metadata table counts.
98: 
99: ### Key Components
100: - **`convert_hints.py`**: the conversion tool, saved by `tasks.md` T004.
101: - **`replace_block.py`**: replaces the lines from a start marker up to an end marker, and refuses unless each marker occurs once. Used for the orchestrator.
102: - **`mutate.py`**: replaces one exact text that must occur once. Used for the mutation checks.
103: - **`apply_edits.py`**: applies old-text and new-text pairs to a doc, and refuses unless each old text occurs once.
104: - **`strict-census.mjs`**: validates every folder in a list with the orchestrator built in this checkout and prints one row per folder.
105: - **`suite_compare.py`**: compares two suite outputs and allows only the new test file and its tests.
106: - **`placeholder-token-gate.vitest.ts`**: the new test.
107: - **Conductor**: runs every task and reads every output.
108: - **Reviewer**: one read-only `cli-codex` review at phase close.
109: 
110: ### Data Flow
111: Templates are converted and stamped. A scaffold made from them carries tokens and the v2.3 stamp. The orchestrator reads the stamp and the spec status for each doc and returns pass, warn or error for `PLACEHOLDER_FILLED`. The test drives the orchestrator through `validate.sh` and the shell rule through `bash -c`, and compares them.

59: A stamp-gated lifecycle. The template stamp says which contract a doc was written under. The validator keeps the old strict verdict for any doc without the new stamp and applies the Draft lifecycle only to docs that carry it.
60: 
61: ### Facts read from the tree while this plan was written
62: 
63: - `validate.sh` runs the compiled `runtime/dist/lib/validation/orchestrator.js`, never the shell rules, for the rule `PLACEHOLDER_FILLED`. The orchestrator lists it in `nativeRuleIds`, and `runRegistryShellRules` skips every rule in that set. The proof is the wording: a v2.3 scaffold validated in a scratch copy printed `unfilled value token(s) in a Draft packet`, which is the new orchestrator message, and not the shell message.
64: - `validate.sh` exits 3 with the text `compiled validation orchestrator is stale` when `runtime/dist` is older than its source. So the TypeScript edit is invisible until `npm run build` runs under `runtime/`.
65: - `rules/check-placeholders.sh` still matters. The harness `runtime/cli/tests/test-validation-extended.sh` sources it in the category `Individual Rule: PLACEHOLDER_FILLED (check-placeholders.sh)`, and its header says it mirrors the orchestrator.
66: - A warning does not fail strict. The orchestrator sets `passed: summary.errors === 0`.
67: - `create.sh` function `finalize_scaffold_templates` replaces `[NAME]`, `[YYYY-MM-DD]`, `[Feature Name]` and `[###-feature-name]` and strips ` [template:...]` with `perl`. Function `ensure_template_source_near_top` moves the stamp line below the frontmatter. The stamp text, including its version, comes from the template.
68: - `templates/spec-kit-docs.json` lists a version per template, and `runtime/cli/tests/template-version-parity.vitest.ts` fails when a manifest version differs from the template stamp.
69: - `runtime/cli/tests/scaffold-golden-snapshots.vitest.ts` renders these templates and compares them with `runtime/cli/tests/snapshots/scaffold-golden-snapshots.vitest.ts.snap`. Without `-u` it fails after conversion on four tests.
70: - The orchestrator reads every authored doc that is present. The shell rule reads only `spec.md`, `plan.md`, `tasks.md` and `decision-record.md`. This difference exists today and the plan keeps it for older docs (ADR-007).
71: 
72: ### Frozen definitions
73: 
74: **Hint.** A bracketed text that matches `\[[A-Za-z/][^]\[]{2,}\]`. The slash lets the score cells `[/25]`, `[/20]` and `[/15]` count. Phase 1 counted with a letter-only start, so on the same Level 2 scaffold it saw 97 occurrences and this regex sees 101.
75: 
76: **Conversion rule.** The script `convert_hints.py` turns a hint into `[YOUR_VALUE_HERE: ` followed by the hint text and `]`. The text keeps its case. It skips five cases:
77: 1. A line inside a fenced code block.
78: 2. Text inside an inline code span.
79: 3. Text followed directly by `(`, which is a link.
80: 4. The five scaffolder texts `NAME`, `Feature Name`, `YYYY-MM-DD`, `###-feature-name` and `1/2/3/3+`, and any text that starts with `template:`. `create.sh` replaces or strips them, so a token there would stay in every scaffold.
81: 5. A text that already starts with `YOUR_VALUE_HERE`.
82: 
83: **Counts the conversion must give.** Converted per file: `spec.md.tmpl` 96, `plan.md.tmpl` 90, `tasks.md.tmpl` 7, `implementation-summary.md.tmpl` 11, `acceptance-criteria.md.tmpl` 10, so 214 in all. The total hint count of each file does not change, because a token is itself a hint under this regex. The bare hints left are exactly the ones in `tasks.md` T011.
84: 
85: **Stamp.** The 7 stamp lines of those five templates change from `| v2.2 -->` to `| v2.3 -->`: 3 in `spec.md.tmpl` and 1 each in the other four. The five manifest entries change the same way.
86: 
87: **Gate stamp.** A doc carries the gate stamp when one of its first 70 lines matches `<!-- SPECKIT_TEMPLATE_SOURCE: <names> | vMAJOR.MINOR -->` with MAJOR above 2, or MAJOR 2 and MINOR 3 or more. A doc with an older stamp or none does not.
88: 
89: **Lifecycle.**
90: 
91: | Doc | Status in `spec.md` | Unfilled `[YOUR_VALUE_HERE:` token | `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION:` | Strict result |
92: |-----|---------------------|------------------------------------|-------------------------|---------------|
93: | Gate stamp | Draft | warning | error | passes when nothing else errors |
94: | Gate stamp | any other value or none | error | error | fails |
95: | No gate stamp | any value | error | error | fails, as before |
96: 
97: Draft means the cell holds the word Draft, ignoring case, bold marks, backticks, outer quotes, trailing punctuation and repeated spaces. The first Status row of the metadata table counts.
98: 
99: ### Key Components
100: - **`convert_hints.py`**: the conversion tool, saved by `tasks.md` T004.
101: - **`replace_block.py`**: replaces the lines from a start marker up to an end marker, and refuses unless each marker occurs once. Used for the orchestrator.
102: - **`mutate.py`**: replaces one exact text that must occur once. Used for the mutation checks.
103: - **`apply_edits.py`**: applies old-text and new-text pairs to a doc, and refuses unless each old text occurs once.
104: - **`strict-census.mjs`**: validates every folder in a list with the orchestrator built in this checkout and prints one row per folder.
105: - **`suite_compare.py`**: compares two suite outputs and allows only the new test file and its tests.
106: - **`placeholder-token-gate.vitest.ts`**: the new test.
107: - **Conductor**: runs every task and reads every output.
108: - **Reviewer**: one read-only `cli-codex` review at phase close.
109: 
110: ### Data Flow
111: Templates are converted and stamped. A scaffold made from them carries tokens and the v2.3 stamp. The orchestrator reads the stamp and the spec status for each doc and returns pass, warn or error for `PLACEHOLDER_FILLED`. The test drives the orchestrator through `validate.sh` and the shell rule through `bash -c`, and compares them.
112: <!-- /ANCHOR:architecture -->

<!-- ANCHOR:problem -->
## 2. PROBLEM & PURPOSE

### Problem Statement
A DeepSeek V4.1 Flash worker that authors a spec packet from the system-spec-kit templates leaves scaffold hints in place and still passes `validate.sh --strict`. A fresh Level 2 scaffold holds 97 bracketed hint occurrences and validates clean. The hand-written examples the worker imitates carry leaked description text and stale lines. The authoring guidance is a 1,200-line template guide that a weak model cannot follow in one pass. Together these let a swarm produce packets that look finished and are not.

### Purpose
Make the templates, the examples, the validator and the authoring docs good enough that a DeepSeek V4.1 Flash swarm authors a valid, filled packet without a frontier model correcting it. Phase 001 measures the starting point and the last phase measures the result, so the claim rests on numbers.

> **Phase-parent note:** This spec.md is the ONLY authored document at the parent level. All detailed planning, task breakdowns, checklists, and decisions live in the child phase folders listed in the Phase Documentation Map below. This keeps the parent from drifting stale as phases execute and pivot.
<!-- /ANCHOR:problem -->

---

<!-- ANCHOR:scope -->
## 3. SCOPE

### In Scope
- Repair the known template, example and reference defects, found by a census and fixed by exact text swap.
- Gate unfilled placeholders on new docs only, through a template version marker.
- Add a one-line fill instruction with a good and a weak example to each core template section.
- Add a short authoring card and route the skill router to it.
- Check and update the speckit and doctor commands and the doc-authoring agents such as markdown.
- Align the playbook, catalog and READMEs of system-spec-kit, then run the playbooks in a disposable worktree.
- Measure the authoring baseline before any change and again at the end.
- One write-recipe fix, tracked as a child of the earlier write-recipe series.

### Out of Scope
- Any change to `sk-prompt`. All logic lives in system-spec-kit.
- Any change that alters the verdict for an existing packet, because external-repo users would break on `/doctor:update`.
- Measuring models other than DeepSeek V4.1 Flash max for the benchmark.
- Committing or pushing. Both stay with the operator.

### Files to Change

| File Path | Change Type | Phase | Description |
|-----------|-------------|-------|-------------|
| `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/examples/**` | Modify | 002, 004 | Example descriptions, stale lines, skeleton alignment |
| `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/references/**` | Modify | 002, 005, 006 | Style guide, checklist, template guide, new card |
| `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/core/*.tmpl` | Modify | 003, 004, 005 | Token form, v2.3 marker, fill guidance, task `Verify:` slot |
| `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/rules/check-placeholders.sh` and its TypeScript mirror | Modify | 003 | Versioned placeholder gate |
| `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/SKILL.md`, `leaf-manifest.json`, `leaf-aliases.json` | Modify | 005 | Router loads the card |
| `.skilled/commands/speckit/`, `.skilled/commands/doctor/` speckit entries, `.skilled/agents/markdown.md` and other doc-authoring agents | Modify | 006 | Commands and agents match the new templates, gate and card |
| `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/` guard scripts | Create | 004, 005 | Example drift guard and card sync guard |
| `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/manual-testing-playbook/`, `feature-catalog/`, READMEs | Modify | 007 | Scenarios and docs for the new behavior |
| `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/benchmark/reports/` | Create | 008, 009 | Playbook run report and benchmark report |
| `specs/system-speckit/041-write-recipe-fixes/006-fix-write-recipe-move-destination/` | Create | 041-006 | Write-recipe move destination fix |

### Launch preconditions

The operator meets all four before the first phase runs. The conductor records each as met in `goal.md` section 4 and stops when one is not.

1. **Workspace.** The operator chooses A) a git worktree or B) the current branch, following `sk-git`. The conductor never chooses. The chosen path becomes `WORKTREE` in `goal.md` section 4.
2. **Provider login.** `opencode2 models --standalone` lists `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`. A billing or region refusal stops the run.
3. **Lane authorization.** At most 3 parallel DeepSeek lanes and never two on one file. The operator has already given this.
4. **Conductor placement.** The conductor is a DeepSeek session that runs outside OpenCode, because `cli-opencode` refuses self-dispatch and forbids a nested `opencode run`.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Guard: every hand-written example keeps the anchor skeleton of the template it
# imitates and a description a reader can use. Read-only: it prints one line per
# failure and exits 1, and changes nothing.
set -uo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../.." && pwd)"
TEMPLATES="$ROOT/templates"
RENDERER="$ROOT/runtime/cli/templates/inline-gate-renderer.sh"
status=0

fail() {
  printf 'FAIL %s: %s\n' "$1" "$2"
  status=1
}

for dir in "$TEMPLATES"/examples/level-*; do
  level="${dir##*/level-}"
  for example in "$dir"/*.md; do
    name="$(basename "$example")"
    doc="${name%.md}"
    template="$TEMPLATES/core/$name.tmpl"
    [[ -f "$template" ]] || template="$TEMPLATES/addons/$name.tmpl"
    [[ -f "$template" ]] || continue

    desc="$(awk '/^description:/{sub(/^description:[[:space:]]*/,""); print; exit}' "$example")"
    bare="${desc%\"}"
    bare="${bare#\"}"
    [[ "$bare" == *"-->"* ]] && fail "$example" "description holds an HTML comment tail"
    [[ "$bare" =~ ^[a-z] ]] && fail "$example" "description starts lowercase"
    [[ "$bare" == *. ]] || fail "$example" "description does not end with a period"

    template_anchors="$(bash "$RENDERER" --level "$level" "$template" \
      | rg -o 'ANCHOR:[a-z0-9-]+' | sed 's/ANCHOR://' | sort -u)"
    example_anchors="$(rg -o 'ANCHOR:[a-z0-9-]+' "$example" | sed 's/ANCHOR://' | sort -u)"

    if [[ "$doc" == "decision-record" ]]; then
      template_anchors="$(printf '%s\n' "$template_anchors" | rg '^adr-001' || true)"
      example_anchors="$(printf '%s\n' "$example_anchors" | rg '^adr-001' || true)"
    fi

    missing="$(comm -23 <(printf '%s\n' "$template_anchors" | sed '/^$/d') \
                         <(printf '%s\n' "$example_anchors" | sed '/^$/d') | tr '\n' ' ')"
    extra="$(comm -13 <(printf '%s\n' "$template_anchors" | sed '/^$/d') \
                       <(printf '%s\n' "$example_anchors" | sed '/^$/d') | tr '\n' ' ')"
    [[ -n "${missing// /}" ]] && fail "$example" "missing anchors: $missing"
    [[ -n "${extra// /}" ]] && fail "$example" "extra anchors: $extra"

    opens="$(rg -c '<!-- ANCHOR:' "$example" || echo 0)"
    closes="$(rg -c '<!-- /ANCHOR:' "$example" || echo 0)"
    [[ "$opens" == "$closes" ]] || fail "$example" "anchor count $opens open and $closes close"
  done
done

[[ $status -eq 0 ]] && echo "EXAMPLE_DRIFT_OK"
exit $status

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Guard: every hand-written example keeps the template's required anchors, adds no
# anchor the template does not allow, and carries a description a reader can use.
# Read-only. Prints one line per failure and exits 1.
set -uo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../.." && pwd)"
TEMPLATES="$ROOT/templates"
UTIL="$ROOT/runtime/cli/utils/template-structure.js"
EXAMPLES="${1:-$TEMPLATES/examples}"
status=0

fail() {
  printf 'FAIL %s: %s\n' "$1" "$2"
  status=1
}

for dir in "$EXAMPLES"/level-*; do
  level="${dir##*/level-}"
  for example in "$dir"/*.md; do
    name="$(basename "$example")"
    desc="$(awk '/^description:/{sub(/^description:[[:space:]]*/,""); print; exit}' "$example")"
    bare="${desc%\"}"
    bare="${bare#\"}"
    [[ "$bare" == *"-->"* ]] && fail "$example" "description holds an HTML comment tail"
    [[ "$bare" =~ ^[a-z] ]] && fail "$example" "description starts lowercase"
    [[ "$bare" == *. ]] || fail "$example" "description does not end with a period"

    report="$(node "$UTIL" compare "$level" "$name" "$example" anchors 2>&1)"
    rc=$?
    if [[ $rc -ne 0 ]]; then
      fail "$example" "template-structure compare exited $rc"
      continue
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "$report" | rg '^(missing_anchor|extra_anchor)' \
      | while read -r kind anchor; do
          printf 'FAIL %s: %s %s\n' "$example" "$kind" "$anchor"
        done
    printf '%s\n' "$report" | rg -q '^(missing_anchor|extra_anchor)' && status=1
  done
done

[[ $status -eq 0 ]] && echo "EXAMPLE_DRIFT_OK"
exit $status

### The fill line format (frozen)

One physical line, placed immediately below the section heading.

```text
<!-- FILL: <instruction> GOOD: <good example> WEAK: <weak example> -->
```

When the table below has `-` in both the Good and the Weak cell, the line is:

```text
<!-- FILL: <instruction> -->
```

Rules for the text inside the line:
- The instruction is one imperative sentence and ends with a period.
- No cell contains `[`, `]`, `-->`, `;` or an em dash.
- The line is never wrapped. It is one line in the template source.
- The good example is concrete and short. The weak example is the failure a weak model produces: vague, generic or a restatement of the heading.
- The model deletes the line when it fills the section. A line left behind is not a placeholder, so it never fails the gate.

### The running example (frozen)

Every good and weak example is about one feature so the examples read as one packet:

**Add a `--quiet` flag to `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/recommend-level.sh`.** With the flag the script prints only the `Recommended Level:` line. Without it the output is unchanged and holds 17 lines.

Do not change the example. A second feature would make the examples incoherent.

### Drift guard contract

`runtime/cli/spec/check-example-drift.sh` is read-only. It runs the contract command on every example, fails on any `missing_anchor` or `extra_anchor`, and checks the description:

1. The description does not contain `-->`.
2. The first character is not lowercase.
3. The last character is a period.

The full source is in `tasks.md` T010. It prints `EXAMPLE_DRIFT_OK` and exits 0 when every example passes. It prints one `FAIL` line per problem and exits 1 otherwise.

It is wired as `runtime/cli/tests/example-drift.vitest.ts`, because `package.json` has no `check-` script and every existing guard is a vitest test. Evidence: `rg -n 'check-' package.json` exited 1, and `template-structure.vitest.ts` is a vitest guard.

### Data Flow
Lane A and Lane B edit templates. Lane C aligns examples and writes both guards. The conductor regenerates the snapshots once, then runs the fill test, the golden test, the drift guard and the validator. A failure returns to the lane that owns the file.

## AI EXECUTION PROTOCOL

Written for the executing swarm. Follow each rule as written. Where a rule and your own judgment disagree, follow the rule and record the disagreement in `goal.md` section 4.

### Roles
- **Conductor**: one DeepSeek V4.1 Flash max session that is not itself running inside OpenCode. It dispatches workers, runs every verify command, owns the snapshot file and edits only this phase folder.
- **Worker**: one `opencode2 run` dispatch on `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max`. One worker does one lane, then stops.
- **Reviewer**: one read-only frontier review through `cli-codex` at phase close. It writes nothing.

### Pre-Task Checklist
- [ ] Read this phase's `spec.md`, this plan and `tasks.md` before the first dispatch
- [ ] Read `.skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/SKILL.md` sections 3 and 4 before composing the first worker command
- [ ] Confirm the working directory is the build worktree recorded in `../goal.md` section 4
- [ ] Confirm `opencode2 models --standalone` lists `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`
- [ ] Save every brief to `scratch/briefs/<task-id>.txt` before dispatching it

### Execution Rules

| Rule | Requirement |
|------|-------------|
| TASK-SEQ | Run tasks in ID order. Tasks marked `[P]` may run together, at most three at once, and only when no two write the same file |
| TASK-SCOPE | A worker writes only the paths under ALLOWED WRITE PATHS in its brief |
| TASK-VERIFY | The conductor runs the task's verify command and reads both its output and its exit status before marking the task `[x]` |
| TASK-LOCATE | Find text by its exact content, never by a line number |
| TASK-BANNED | Workers never run `git commit`, `git push`, `git checkout`, `git switch`, `git branch`, `git reset`, `git stash`, `generate-context.js` or `/speckit:save` |

## L3: ARCHITECTURE DECISION RECORD

### ADR-001: Put the guidance in an HTML comment below the heading

**Status**: Accepted

**Context**: The guidance must not trip phase 003's token gate, must work for a prose paragraph, a table cell and a checklist item, and must not break the header comparison in `template-structure.js`.

**Decision**: Each section carries one ordinary HTML comment on its own line, immediately below the heading: `<!-- FILL: ... -->`. The existing `[YOUR_VALUE_HERE: ...]` tokens stay where they are and remain field-level prompts.

**Consequences**:
- The gate ignores the line because it holds no token syntax.
- The line renders into the scaffold but is invisible on the rendered page.
- A model that leaves the line behind leaves a harmless comment, not an unfilled placeholder.

**Alternatives Rejected**:
- Inside the token: a long instruction inside a table cell breaks the table, and a checklist item cannot hold it.
- On the heading line: `template-structure.js` compares heading text, so a comment in the heading would make every filled document differ from its contract.
- A separate guide file: a weak model fills the section in front of it and does not follow a pointer to a second file.

### ADR-002: One fill line per section, not per hint

**Status**: Accepted

**Context**: The four core templates hold 214 hints after phase 003 and 64 sections. One line per hint would repeat the same instruction many times and make the plan unreadable.

**Decision**: One line per `## ` section. It names the one action for the section. The tokens inside the section stay as field-level prompts.

**Consequences**:
- The plan is bounded and the model reads one instruction per section.
- A section with eight tokens still has one governing instruction.

**Alternatives Rejected**:
- Per-token guidance: repetitive, and it hides the section-level action in a crowd of field prompts.

### ADR-003: Delegate anchor comparison to the template contract

**Status**: Accepted

**Context**: A hand-rolled anchor set comparison would duplicate the contract and drift from the validator.

**Decision**: `check-example-drift.sh` calls `node runtime/cli/utils/template-structure.js compare <level> <doc> <example> anchors` and fails on any `missing_anchor` or `extra_anchor` line.

**Consequences**:
- The guard and the validator read one source of truth.
- The guard inherits the contract's dynamic ADR handling for `decision-record.md`.

**Alternatives Rejected**:
- A bash set difference: it would need its own copy of the required and optional lists.

### ADR-004: Examples satisfy required anchors and add no extra anchor

**Status**: Accepted

**Context**: The contract marks some anchors optional, and an example may legitimately omit an optional section. Full equality would force optional sections into every example and would fight the dynamic ADR anchors.

**Decision**: An example must carry every required anchor and no anchor outside the template's allowed set. Optional anchors may be absent.

**Consequences**:
- The alignment table is 14 files, not 24.
- A missing optional section is not drift.

**Alternatives Rejected**:
- Full set equality: it would force `affected-surfaces` and the L3+ workstream sections into every example.

### ADR-005: Regenerate the golden snapshots once, by the conductor

**Status**: Accepted

**Context**: The golden test stores 25 renders. Two lanes edit templates, and one snapshot file cannot take two writers.

**Decision**: Lanes A and B finish first. The conductor runs `npx vitest run runtime/cli/tests/scaffold-golden-snapshots.vitest.ts -u` once, then reruns without `-u`.

**Consequences**:
- One snapshot diff covers every template change.
- No lane writes the snapshot file.

**Alternatives Rejected**:
- Each lane updates the snapshots: two lanes would write one file, which breaks the frozen lane rule.

### ADR-006: Optional sections may be deleted, required sections get N/A

**Status**: Accepted

**Context**: A weak model invents a feature flag, an OWASP review and an uptime target for a documentation packet. The contract decides which sections may disappear.

**Decision**: The fill line for an optional section says either `N/A` with one reason or delete the section. The fill line for a required section says `N/A` with one reason and never says delete.

**Consequences**:
- A packet with no service stops inventing an uptime target.
- A Level 3+ compliance checkpoint stays present because the contract requires it.

**Alternatives Rejected**:
- Remove the generic sections from the templates: the Level 3+ contract requires three of them.

### Drift guard contract

`runtime/cli/spec/check-example-drift.sh` is read-only. It runs the contract command on every example, fails on any `missing_anchor` or `extra_anchor`, and checks the description:

1. The description does not contain `-->`.
2. The first character is not lowercase.
3. The last character is a period.

The full source is in `tasks.md` T010. It prints `EXAMPLE_DRIFT_OK` and exits 0 when every example passes. It prints one `FAIL` line per problem and exits 1 otherwise.

It is wired as `runtime/cli/tests/example-drift.vitest.ts`, because `package.json` has no `check-` script and every existing guard is a vitest test. Evidence: `rg -n 'check-' package.json` exited 1, and `template-structure.vitest.ts` is a vitest guard.

### Data Flow
Lane A and Lane B edit templates. Lane C aligns examples and writes both guards. The conductor regenerates the snapshots once, then runs the fill test, the golden test, the drift guard and the validator. A failure returns to the lane that owns the file.

## AI EXECUTION PROTOCOL

Written for the executing swarm. Follow each rule as written. Where a rule and your own judgment disagree, follow the rule and record the disagreement in `goal.md` section 4.

### Roles
- **Conductor**: one DeepSeek V4.1 Flash max session that is not itself running inside OpenCode. It dispatches workers, runs every verify command, owns the snapshot file and edits only this phase folder.
- **Worker**: one `opencode2 run` dispatch on `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max`. One worker does one lane, then stops.
- **Reviewer**: one read-only frontier review through `cli-codex` at phase close. It writes nothing.

### Pre-Task Checklist
- [ ] Read this phase's `spec.md`, this plan and `tasks.md` before the first dispatch
- [ ] Read `.skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/SKILL.md` sections 3 and 4 before composing the first worker command
- [ ] Confirm the working directory is the build worktree recorded in `../goal.md` section 4
- [ ] Confirm `opencode2 models --standalone` lists `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`
- [ ] Save every brief to `scratch/briefs/<task-id>.txt` before dispatching it

### Execution Rules

| Rule | Requirement |
|------|-------------|
| TASK-SEQ | Run tasks in ID order. Tasks marked `[P]` may run together, at most three at once, and only when no two write the same file |
| TASK-SCOPE | A worker writes only the paths under ALLOWED WRITE PATHS in its brief |
| TASK-VERIFY | The conductor runs the task's verify command and reads both its output and its exit status before marking the task `[x]` |
| TASK-LOCATE | Find text by its exact content, never by a line number |
| TASK-BANNED | Workers never run `git commit`, `git push`, `git checkout`, `git switch`, `git branch`, `git reset`, `git stash`, `generate-context.js` or `/speckit:save` |

### Worker Brief Skeleton

Every brief starts with this block, word for word, with the two paths filled in:

```text
GATE 3 IS PRE-RESOLVED. DO NOT ASK THE DOCUMENTATION-SCOPE QUESTION.

You are a non-interactive dispatched worker. AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 and
SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0 are set in your environment, which this repository's AGENTS.md
defines as the autonomous child-dispatch exemption: the spec-folder question is pre-resolved
and MUST NOT be asked. No answer can reach you, because nobody is at a prompt.

Your write authority is already bound. The spec folder is:
  specs/system-speckit/054-weak-model-spec-authoring/004-template-section-fill-guidance

Proceed directly to the work. Do not print A/B/C/D options. Do not stop to confirm anything.
A failed edit match means a stale anchor: re-read the file and retry; halt only after three
failures on the same file.
Your task is complete only when files exist on disk and the verification command has been run.

ROLE: You are a documentation editor. You copy text from plan.md into templates, and you
run read-only checks. Your output is checked by a script.

ALLOWED WRITE PATHS:
  <the files this lane owns>

BANNED OPERATIONS: git commit, git push, git checkout, git switch, git branch, git reset,
git stash, rm, mv, create.sh, generate-context.js, /speckit:save, and any edit to a file not
listed under ALLOWED WRITE PATHS.
```

The role line is a focused persona summary in place of a full agent file, the small-context exception that `cli-opencode` rule 18 allows. It is declared here as that exception.

### Dispatch Command

```bash
cd "$WORKTREE" && SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0 AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 opencode2 run --standalone \
  -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max --format json \
  "$(cat "$PHASE/scratch/briefs/$TASK.txt")" </dev/null > "$PHASE/scratch/runs/$TASK.jsonl" 2>&1 &
PID=$!; wait "$PID"; kill -9 "$PID" 2>/dev/null; pkill -9 -P "$PID" 2>/dev/null
```

`PHASE` is this folder's path and `WORKTREE` is the build worktree. Never kill by a name pattern. Kill only the captured PID.

### Status Reporting Format

`[T###] DONE | BLOCKED - one line of evidence`, written as a row in the progress table of `goal.md` section 4.

### Blocked Task Protocol
1. Restore any file the task changed with `git restore --source=<start commit> -- <file>`.
2. Mark the task `[B]` in `tasks.md` with the failing command and the first line of its output.
3. Re-dispatch at most twice with the brief corrected for what failed. After the third failure on the same task, leave it `[B]` and continue with the next task.
4. Stop the phase when two tasks are blocked, and write `STOP` with both task IDs in `goal.md` section 4.
<!-- /ANCHOR:ai-execution -->

## L3: ARCHITECTURE DECISION RECORD

### ADR-001: Put the guidance in an HTML comment below the heading

**Status**: Accepted

**Context**: The guidance must not trip phase 003's token gate, must work for a prose paragraph, a table cell and a checklist item, and must not break the header comparison in `template-structure.js`.

**Decision**: Each section carries one ordinary HTML comment on its own line, immediately below the heading: `<!-- FILL: ... -->`. The existing `[YOUR_VALUE_HERE: ...]` tokens stay where they are and remain field-level prompts.

**Consequences**:
- The gate ignores the line because it holds no token syntax.
- The line renders into the scaffold but is invisible on the rendered page.
- A model that leaves the line behind leaves a harmless comment, not an unfilled placeholder.

**Alternatives Rejected**:
- Inside the token: a long instruction inside a table cell breaks the table, and a checklist item cannot hold it.
- On the heading line: `template-structure.js` compares heading text, so a comment in the heading would make every filled document differ from its contract.
- A separate guide file: a weak model fills the section in front of it and does not follow a pointer to a second file.

### ADR-002: One fill line per section, not per hint

**Status**: Accepted

**Context**: The four core templates hold 214 hints after phase 003 and 64 sections. One line per hint would repeat the same instruction many times and make the plan unreadable.

**Decision**: One line per `## ` section. It names the one action for the section. The tokens inside the section stay as field-level prompts.

**Consequences**:
- The plan is bounded and the model reads one instruction per section.
- A section with eight tokens still has one governing instruction.

**Alternatives Rejected**:
- Per-token guidance: repetitive, and it hides the section-level action in a crowd of field prompts.

### ADR-003: Delegate anchor comparison to the template contract

**Status**: Accepted

**Context**: A hand-rolled anchor set comparison would duplicate the contract and drift from the validator.

**Decision**: `check-example-drift.sh` calls `node runtime/cli/utils/template-structure.js compare <level> <doc> <example> anchors` and fails on any `missing_anchor` or `extra_anchor` line.

**Consequences**:
- The guard and the validator read one source of truth.
- The guard inherits the contract's dynamic ADR handling for `decision-record.md`.

**Alternatives Rejected**:
- A bash set difference: it would need its own copy of the required and optional lists.

### ADR-004: Examples satisfy required anchors and add no extra anchor

**Status**: Accepted

**Context**: The contract marks some anchors optional, and an example may legitimately omit an optional section. Full equality would force optional sections into every example and would fight the dynamic ADR anchors.

**Decision**: An example must carry every required anchor and no anchor outside the template's allowed set. Optional anchors may be absent.

**Consequences**:
- The alignment table is 14 files, not 24.
- A missing optional section is not drift.

**Alternatives Rejected**:
- Full set equality: it would force `affected-surfaces` and the L3+ workstream sections into every example.

### ADR-005: Regenerate the golden snapshots once, by the conductor

**Status**: Accepted

**Context**: The golden test stores 25 renders. Two lanes edit templates, and one snapshot file cannot take two writers.

**Decision**: Lanes A and B finish first. The conductor runs `npx vitest run runtime/cli/tests/scaffold-golden-snapshots.vitest.ts -u` once, then reruns without `-u`.

**Consequences**:
- One snapshot diff covers every template change.
- No lane writes the snapshot file.

**Alternatives Rejected**:
- Each lane updates the snapshots: two lanes would write one file, which breaks the frozen lane rule.

### ADR-006: Optional sections may be deleted, required sections get N/A

**Status**: Accepted

**Context**: A weak model invents a feature flag, an OWASP review and an uptime target for a documentation packet. The contract decides which sections may disappear.

**Decision**: The fill line for an optional section says either `N/A` with one reason or delete the section. The fill line for a required section says `N/A` with one reason and never says delete.

**Consequences**:
- A packet with no service stops inventing an uptime target.
- A Level 3+ compliance checkpoint stays present because the contract requires it.

**Alternatives Rejected**:
- Remove the generic sections from the templates: the Level 3+ contract requires three of them.

---
title: "Tasks: Phase 4: template-section-fill-guidance"
description: "Task Format: T### [P?] Description (file path). Each task names a verify command and the output that proves it."
trigger_phrases:
  - "template section fill guidance tasks"
  - "example drift guard source"
  - "fill guidance test source"
importance_tier: "normal"
contextType: "general"
---
<!-- SPECKIT_TEMPLATE_SOURCE: tasks-core | v2.2 -->
# Tasks: Phase 4: template-section-fill-guidance

<!-- SPECKIT_LEVEL: 3 -->

---

<!-- ANCHOR:notation -->
## Task Notation

| Prefix | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `[ ]` | Pending |
| `[x]` | Completed |
| `[P]` | Parallelizable |
| `[B]` | Blocked |

**Task Format**: `T### [P?] Description (file path)`, then `Verify:` with the command whose output proves the task.

Shell variables used below, set once by the conductor:
- `WORKTREE`: the build worktree path recorded in `../goal.md` section 4.
- `PHASE`: `$WORKTREE/specs/system-speckit/054-weak-model-spec-authoring/004-template-section-fill-guidance`
- `S`: `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit`
- `START`: the commit hash recorded by T002.
<!-- /ANCHOR:notation -->

---

<!-- ANCHOR:phase-1 -->
## Phase 1: Setup

- [ ] T001 Check tools and the phase 003 result (no file). Run `node --version`, `cd "$S" && ./node_modules/.bin/vitest --version`, `which rg awk git`, and `rg -c 'YOUR_VALUE_HERE' "$S/templates/core/spec.md.tmpl"`. Verify: the first two lines hold a version, the next three hold a path, and the last line is a number above 0.

- [ ] T002 Record the start state (`goal.md`, `scratch/baseline/status-start.txt`, `scratch/baseline/suite-start.txt`). Run `git -C "$WORKTREE" rev-parse HEAD`, write the hash into `goal.md` section 4 as `Start commit`, run `git -C "$WORKTREE" status --porcelain > "$PHASE/scratch/baseline/status-start.txt"`, then run `npm --prefix "$WORKTREE/$S" test > "$PHASE/scratch/baseline/suite-start.txt" 2>&1; echo "exit=$?" >> "$PHASE/scratch/baseline/suite-start.txt"`. Verify: `grep -c 'Start commit' "$PHASE/goal.md"` prints `1` and `tail -1 "$PHASE/scratch/baseline/suite-start.txt"` prints an `exit=` line.

- [ ] T003 Record the anchor baseline (`scratch/baseline/anchor-counts.txt`). Run this from `$WORKTREE`. Verify: `wc -l < "$PHASE/scratch/baseline/anchor-counts.txt"` prints `16`, `grep -c '^1 spec 7$'` prints `1` and `grep -c '^3+ plan 17$'` prints `1`.

  ```bash
  : > "$PHASE/scratch/baseline/anchor-counts.txt"
  for lvl in 1 2 3 3+; do
    for doc in spec plan tasks implementation-summary; do
      n=$(bash "$S/runtime/cli/templates/inline-gate-renderer.sh" --level "$lvl" "$S/templates/core/$doc.md.tmpl" | grep -c '<!-- ANCHOR:')
      echo "$lvl $doc $n" >> "$PHASE/scratch/baseline/anchor-counts.txt"
    done
  done
  ```

  The frozen result is:

  ```text
  1 spec 7
  1 plan 7
  1 tasks 6
  1 implementation-summary 6
  2 spec 10
  2 plan 11
  2 tasks 15
  2 implementation-summary 6
  3 spec 7
  3 plan 14
  3 tasks 21
  3 implementation-summary 6
  3+ spec 11
  3+ plan 17
  3+ tasks 21
  3+ implementation-summary 6
  ```

- [ ] T004 Record the golden baseline (no file). Run `cd "$S" && ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run runtime/cli/tests/scaffold-golden-snapshots.vitest.ts --config vitest.config.ts`. Verify: the output contains `Tests  12 passed (12)`.

- [ ] T005 Write the two guards and the fill test (`$S/runtime/cli/spec/check-example-drift.sh`, `$S/runtime/cli/tests/example-drift.vitest.ts`, `$S/runtime/cli/tests/template-fill-guidance.vitest.ts`). Write the three files exactly as they appear in the code blocks below, then run `chmod +x "$S/runtime/cli/spec/check-example-drift.sh"`. Verify: `bash -n "$S/runtime/cli/spec/check-example-drift.sh"` exits 0 and `ls` prints the three paths.

  `check-example-drift.sh` source:

  ```bash
  #!/usr/bin/env bash
  # Guard: every hand-written example keeps the template's required anchors, adds no
  # anchor the template does not allow, and carries a description a reader can use.
  # Read-only. Prints one line per failure and exits 1.
  set -uo pipefail

  ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../.." && pwd)"
  TEMPLATES="$ROOT/templates"
  UTIL="$ROOT/runtime/cli/utils/template-structure.js"
  EXAMPLES="${1:-$TEMPLATES/examples}"
  status=0

  fail() {
    printf 'FAIL %s: %s\n' "$1" "$2"
    status=1
  }

  for dir in "$EXAMPLES"/level-*; do
    level="${dir##*/level-}"
    for example in "$dir"/*.md; do
      name="$(basename "$example")"
      desc="$(awk '/^description:/{sub(/^description:[[:space:]]*/,""); print; exit}' "$example")"
      bare="${desc%\"}"
      bare="${bare#\"}"
      [[ "$bare" == *"-->"* ]] && fail "$example" "description holds an HTML comment tail"
      [[ "$bare" =~ ^[a-z] ]] && fail "$example" "description starts lowercase"
      [[ "$bare" == *. ]] || fail "$example" "description does not end with a period"

      report="$(node "$UTIL" compare "$level" "$name" "$example" anchors 2>&1)"
      rc=$?
      if [[ $rc -ne 0 ]]; then
        fail "$example" "template-structure compare exited $rc"
        continue
      fi
      printf '%s\n' "$report" | rg '^(missing_anchor|extra_anchor)' \
        | while read -r kind anchor; do
            printf 'FAIL %s: %s %s\n' "$example" "$kind" "$anchor"
          done
      printf '%s\n' "$report" | rg -q '^(missing_anchor|extra_anchor)' && status=1
    done
  done

  [[ $status -eq 0 ]] && echo "EXAMPLE_DRIFT_OK"
  exit $status
  ```

  ```ts
  import fs from 'node:fs';
  import path from 'node:path';
  import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
  import { renderInlineGates, type RenderLevel } from '../templates/inline-gate-renderer';

  const SKILL_ROOT = path.resolve(__dirname, '../../..');
  const TEMPLATE_ROOT = path.join(SKILL_ROOT, 'templates');
  const LEVELS: RenderLevel[] = ['1', '2', '3', '3+'];
  const DOCS = ['spec', 'plan', 'tasks', 'implementation-summary'] as const;

  const ANCHOR_COUNTS: Record<string, number> = {
    '1/spec': 7,
    '1/plan': 7,
    '1/tasks': 6,
    '1/implementation-summary': 6,
    '2/spec': 10,
    '2/plan': 11,
    '2/tasks': 15,
    '2/implementation-summary': 6,
    '3/spec': 7,
    '3/plan': 14,
    '3/tasks': 21,
    '3/implementation-summary': 6,
    '3+/spec': 11,
    '3+/plan': 17,
    '3+/tasks': 21,
    '3+/implementation-summary': 6,
  };

  function sections(markdown: string): Array<{ heading: string; body: string }> {
    const out: Array<{ heading: string; body: string[] }> = [];
    let inFence = false;
    for (const line of markdown.split(/\r?\n/u)) {
      if (/^\s*(`{3}|~~~)/u.test(line)) {
        inFence = !inFence;
      }
      if (!inFence && /^## /u.test(line)) {
        out.push({ heading: line, body: [] });
        continue;
      }
      if (out.length > 0) {
        out[out.length - 1].body.push(line);
      }
    }
    return out.map((section) => ({ heading: section.heading, body: section.body.join('\n') }));
  }

  describe('template section fill guidance', () => {
    for (const level of LEVELS) {
      for (const doc of DOCS) {
        it(`gives every Level ${level} ${doc} section one fill line`, () => {
          const source = fs.readFileSync(path.join(TEMPLATE_ROOT, 'core', `${doc}.md.tmpl`), 'utf8');
          const rendered = renderInlineGates(source, level);
          const anchors = (rendered.match(/<!-- ANCHOR:/gu) ?? []).length;
          expect(anchors, 'anchor count changed').toBe(ANCHOR_COUNTS[`${level}/${doc}`]);
          const parts = sections(rendered);
          expect(parts.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
          for (const part of parts) {
            const fill = part.body.match(/<!-- FILL: .* -->/gu) ?? [];
            expect(fill, `${part.heading} needs one FILL line`).toHaveLength(1);
            const inner = fill[0].slice('<!-- FILL: '.length, -' -->'.length);
            expect(inner).not.toContain('[YOUR_VALUE_HERE:');
            expect(inner).not.toContain('[NEEDS');
            expect(inner).not.toContain('-->');
            expect(inner.trim().endsWith('.')).toBe(true);
          }
        });
      }
    }
  });
  ```

  #!/usr/bin/env bash
  # Guard: every hand-written example keeps the template's required anchors, adds no
  # anchor the template does not allow, and carries a description a reader can use.
  # Read-only. Prints one line per failure and exits 1.
  set -uo pipefail

  ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../.." && pwd)"
  TEMPLATES="$ROOT/templates"
  UTIL="$ROOT/runtime/cli/utils/template-structure.js"
  EXAMPLES="${1:-$TEMPLATES/examples}"
  status=0

  fail() {
    printf 'FAIL %s: %s\n' "$1" "$2"
    status=1
  }

  for dir in "$EXAMPLES"/level-*; do
    level="${dir##*/level-}"
    for example in "$dir"/*.md; do
      name="$(basename "$example")"
      desc="$(awk '/^description:/{sub(/^description:[[:space:]]*/,""); print; exit}' "$example")"
      bare="${desc%\"}"
      bare="${bare#\"}"
      [[ "$bare" == *"-->"* ]] && fail "$example" "description holds an HTML comment tail"
      [[ "$bare" =~ ^[a-z] ]] && fail "$example" "description starts lowercase"
      [[ "$bare" == *. ]] || fail "$example" "description does not end with a period"

      report="$(node "$UTIL" compare "$level" "$name" "$example" anchors 2>&1)"
      rc=$?
      if [[ $rc -ne 0 ]]; then
        fail "$example" "template-structure compare exited $rc"
        continue
      fi
      printf '%s\n' "$report" | rg '^(missing_anchor|extra_anchor)' \
        | while read -r kind anchor; do
            printf 'FAIL %s: %s %s\n' "$example" "$kind" "$anchor"
          done
      printf '%s\n' "$report" | rg -q '^(missing_anchor|extra_anchor)' && status=1
    done
  done

  [[ $status -eq 0 ]] && echo "EXAMPLE_DRIFT_OK"
  exit $status
  ```

  ```ts
  import fs from 'node:fs';
  import path from 'node:path';
  import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
  import { renderInlineGates, type RenderLevel } from '../templates/inline-gate-renderer';

  const SKILL_ROOT = path.resolve(__dirname, '../../..');
  const TEMPLATE_ROOT = path.join(SKILL_ROOT, 'templates');
  const LEVELS: RenderLevel[] = ['1', '2', '3', '3+'];
  const DOCS = ['spec', 'plan', 'tasks', 'implementation-summary'] as const;

  const ANCHOR_COUNTS: Record<string, number> = {
    '1/spec': 7,
    '1/plan': 7,
    '1/tasks': 6,
    '1/implementation-summary': 6,
    '2/spec': 10,
    '2/plan': 11,
    '2/tasks': 15,
    '2/implementation-summary': 6,
    '3/spec': 7,
    '3/plan': 14,
    '3/tasks': 21,
    '3/implementation-summary': 6,
    '3+/spec': 11,
    '3+/plan': 17,
    '3+/tasks': 21,
    '3+/implementation-summary': 6,
  };

  function sections(markdown: string): Array<{ heading: string; body: string }> {
    const out: Array<{ heading: string; body: string[] }> = [];
    let inFence = false;
    for (const line of markdown.split(/\r?\n/u)) {
      if (/^\s*(`{3}|~~~)/u.test(line)) {
        inFence = !inFence;
      }
      if (!inFence && /^## /u.test(line)) {
        out.push({ heading: line, body: [] });
        continue;
      }
      if (out.length > 0) {
        out[out.length - 1].body.push(line);
      }
    }
    return out.map((section) => ({ heading: section.heading, body: section.body.join('\n') }));
  }

  describe('template section fill guidance', () => {
    for (const level of LEVELS) {
      for (const doc of DOCS) {
        it(`gives every Level ${level} ${doc} section one fill line`, () => {
          const source = fs.readFileSync(path.join(TEMPLATE_ROOT, 'core', `${doc}.md.tmpl`), 'utf8');
          const rendered = renderInlineGates(source, level);
          const anchors = (rendered.match(/<!-- ANCHOR:/gu) ?? []).length;
          expect(anchors, 'anchor count changed').toBe(ANCHOR_COUNTS[`${level}/${doc}`]);
          const parts = sections(rendered);
          expect(parts.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
          for (const part of parts) {
            const fill = part.body.match(/<!-- FILL: .* -->/gu) ?? [];
            expect(fill, `${part.heading} needs one FILL line`).toHaveLength(1);
            const inner = fill[0].slice('<!-- FILL: '.length, -' -->'.length);
            expect(inner).not.toContain('[YOUR_VALUE_HERE:');
            expect(inner).not.toContain('[NEEDS');
            expect(inner).not.toContain('-->');
            expect(inner.trim().endsWith('.')).toBe(true);
          }
        });
      }
    }
  });
  ```
